props.title: The Devil Wears Prada

sections.content: The Devil Wears Prada (2006) revolutionized the modern workplace comedy by diving deep into fashion journalism's cutthroat world. Meryl Streep's Miranda Priestly ranks among cinema's most memorable bosses, delivering withering put-downs with surgical precision. The film's influence echoes through later workplace dramas like Late Night (2019) and Morning Glory (2010), establishing a template for ambitious young professionals navigating toxic work environments while maintaining their integrity. Like Working Girl (1988) before it, it examines female power dynamics in corporate America, but with a sharper edge.

sections.content: The film's costume design by Patricia Field created a seismic shift in how fashion was portrayed in cinema. Following Breakfast at Tiffany's (1961) and Clueless (1995), it demonstrated how clothing could be a character itself. The transformation of Andy Sachs from frumpy newcomer to fashion insider sparked countless makeover sequences in later films like Crazy Rich Asians (2018). The $1 million costume budget created looks that influenced real-world fashion for years.

Meryl Streep's performance redefined the "boss from hell" trope, moving beyond simple villainy into complex character study. Unlike the overtly antagonistic bosses in 9 to 5 (1980) or Horrible Bosses (2011), Miranda Priestly is terrifying precisely because she's excellent at her job. Her "cerulean blue sweater" monologue remains a masterclass in establishing power through quiet devastation rather than loud confrontation. SUBHEAD: Fashion in Film and Workplace Evolution

sections.content: The film's examination of work-life balance presaged contemporary discussions about toxic productivity and burnout. Like Up in the Air (2009) and The Intern (2015), it questions the personal cost of professional success. Emily Blunt's breakthrough role as Emily demonstrated how competition and solidarity among women in the workplace could coexist, influencing later films like Bombshell (2019).
